app: Confirm a My Domain is deployed for the org (Setup > Company Settings > My Domain); SP-initiated SSO needs it.
In Setup > Identity > Single Sign-On Settings enable SAML, then New - or 'New from Metadata URL' and paste {idp_metadata_url} to prefill (check your app's current UI).
Manually: Issuer = {idp_entity_id}, Identity Provider Login URL = {idp_sso_url}, upload the Identity Provider Certificate from {idp_cert_url}; optional Identity Provider Logout URL = {idp_slo_url}.
Entity ID: with a My Domain use https://{domain}.my.salesforce.com; without one use https://saml.salesforce.com.

Pick the SAML Identity Type that matches your rollout - 'Assertion contains the Federation ID from the User object' is the usual choice, 'the User's salesforce.com username' works when usernames equal email addresses - and keep 'Identity is in the NameIdentifier element of the Subject statement' (check your app's current UI).
Save, then note the Salesforce Login URL Salesforce displays - that is the ACS URL the FlareID side must allow.
flareid: Add a SAML service provider (Admin > Applications > SAML service providers > New) and apply this template.

Replace {domain} with your My Domain name, or set both the entity ID and ACS URL to the values Salesforce reports after saving (https://saml.salesforce.com / https://login.salesforce.com without a My Domain).

If you chose 'Federation ID' in Salesforce, populate that field on each user and keep NameID format emailAddress only when the Federation ID is the email; otherwise the NameID must equal whatever the identity type compares against.
Leave 'Require signed AuthnRequests' off unless you uploaded a Salesforce request-signing certificate there.
